observation.visible_scene: Against a pure black background, a glowing orange-red bulbous object sits at the left of the frame (roughly constant position, center near x≈100, y≈255). The bulb shows internal vertical ridges/stripes and a bright rim. From its right side a luminous white-to-yellow flame plume jets horizontally to the right, fading to orange-red at its tips.
visible_changes: The bulb on the left stays essentially fixed in position across all frames while the flame plume to its right continuously deforms.
The plume's length and shape fluctuate: it alternates between short stubby blobs (e.g. t≈0.07, 0.27, 0.40) and long stretched, wavy or forked tails (e.g. t≈0.13, 0.33, 0.60, 1.27, 2.14).
The flame's tip oscillates left-right (expansion and contraction of the plume) rather than the whole object translating.
Small detached red ember-like wisps appear and vanish to the right of the main plume in several frames (e.g. t≈0.40, 0.67, 2.14, 2.40, 2.67), then re-merge or fade.
Brightness within the plume flickers, with the white-hot core shifting position along the horizontal axis.
No change in the bulb's internal stripe pattern or overall size is evident.
outside_clip_unknowns: What produces or feeds the flame, and whether the bulb itself moves before/after this cropped segment.
Whether the detached wisps are separate burning fragments or just fading tips of the same plume.
The cause of the plume's wavering (no airflow or operator is visible).
uncertain_details: Camera motion cannot be confirmed because the background is uniform black; the apparent stability of the bulb may reflect either a static camera or coincidental framing.
The intermittent right-side fragments could be occlusion/fade of the plume tip rather than independent objects.
The exact 3D orientation of the bulb (front vs side view) is ambiguous from the silhouette.
